text: This lesson is practice, not new theory. You have six fixed gates and three rotation families from this chapter — now it's time to chain them together, compute real numbers at every step, and build the habit of never assuming how a multi-gate sequence turns out.

Start from ket-zero and apply H, then S, then H again. H on ket-zero gives 0.7071, 0.7071. S leaves the first amplitude alone and multiplies the second by i, giving 0.7071, 0.7071 i. Applying H again produces a final state of 0.5 plus 0.5i, and 0.5 minus 0.5i. Squaring each amplitude's magnitude gives probabilities of 0.5 and 0.5 — matching what plain H alone gives on ket-zero — but the state itself is different, carrying complex amplitudes that a single H never produces. Nothing about this sequence was obvious by inspection; it had to be computed.

Now compare X then Z, against Z then X, both starting from ket-zero. X then Z: X gives ket-one, then Z gives negative ket-one. Z then X: Z leaves ket-zero untouched, then X gives ket-one. Negative ket-one and ket-one are not the same vector — they differ by an overall sign, confirming X and Z don't commute. In this specific case that sign happens to be an unmeasurable global phase, but don't over-generalize: on a superposition, a relative phase from swapping gate order can absolutely change downstream measurement probabilities once another interfering gate is applied.

Every problem in this lab followed the same three-step discipline. Write the starting state as an explicit vector. Apply one gate at a time, computing the full intermediate state — never skip ahead. And only at the end, compute the squared magnitude of each amplitude for the real measurement probabilities, separately asking whether any phase difference you found is global or relative. Every multi-qubit circuit for the rest of this course, CNOT chains, teleportation, superdense coding, is this same process, just with more gates.
That closes out single-qubit gates. Chapter 3 introduces the first two-qubit gate, CNOT, and the start of entanglement.
